questions.q:
Let& $f: \left(- \dfrac{π}{4}, \dfrac{π}{4}\right) \to R$~be defined as,~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\left(1 + \left|sinx\right|\right)3a\left|sinx\right| & , - \dfrac{π}{4} < x < 0 \\ b & , x = 0 \\ e^{cot4x / cot2x} & , 0 < x < \dfrac{π}{4}\end{cases}\right$

If~$f$~is continuous at~$x = 0$~then the value of~$6a + b^{2}$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$If& $f \left(x\right)$~is continuous at point~$x = a,$~then~$\lim_{x \to 0}f \left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f \left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}f\left(x\right)$

From the question, we can say that~$\lim_{x \to 0}f\left(x\right) = b$

And~$\lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}e\dfrac{cot4x}{cot2x} = \lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}e\dfrac{tan2x}{tan4x} = \lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}e\dfrac{\dfrac{tan2x}{2 \times 2$2x}}{\dfrac{tan4x}{4x}} $=e\dfrac{1}{2} =$b$

And~$\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\left(1 + \left|sinx\right|\right)3a\left|sinx\right| = e^{\lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\left[\left(\left|sinx\right|\right)\left(3a\left|sinx\right|\right)\right]} = e^{3a}$

From the above we can say that

$e^{3a} = $e\dfrac{1}{2}

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{1}{6}$⇒ 6a = 1$

So,~ \left($6a + b^{2}\right) = \left(1 + e\right)$

$

Where~ \left[t\right]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Let~$m$ be the number of points where~$f$ is not differentiable and $I = {∫}_{- 2}^{2}f \left(x\right)dx$. Then the ordered pair~\left(m, I\right) is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:

x^{3} - 3x, x \le - 1
2, - 1 5
\right$

Clearly~$f \left(x\right)$~is not differentiable at~$x = 2, 3, 4, 5 ⇒ m = 4$

$I = {∫}_{- 2}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{- 2}^{- 1}\left(x^{3} - 3x\right)dx + {∫}_{- 1}^{2}2 \cdotdx = $\dfrac{27}{4}

Hence the ordered pair is~ \left(4, \dfrac{27}{4}\right)$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{sin\left(a + 2\right)x + sinx}{x} & ; x 0\end{cases}\right$ is continuous at $x = 0$ , then $a + 2b$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left({0}^{-}\right) = \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} \left(\dfrac{sinaxcos2x}{x} + \dfrac{sin2xcosax}{x} + \dfrac{sinx}{x}\right)

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}} \left(acos2x + 2cosax + 1\right)$

$= a + 3$

Also, $f\left(0\right) = b$
$f\left({0}^{+}\right) = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x\dfrac{1}{3}}{x\dfrac{1}{3}} \left(\dfrac{ \left($1 + 3x\$right)\dfrac{1}{3} -$1}${x}\right),$this is~\$left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)$form

Apply~$LH$ Rule~

$⇒ $f\left({0}^{+}\right) =$1$

$∴ a = - 2$

$b = 1$

$∴ a + 2b = 0$

$

questions.q:
Let $f: R \to R$ be defined as

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{
\dfrac{a - bcos2x}{x2}; x< 0
x^{2} + cx + 2; 0 \le x \le 1
2x + 1; x> 1
\right$

If $f$ is continuous everywhere in $R$ and $m$ is the number of points where $f$ is NOT differential then $m + a + b + c$ equals:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$At $x = 1, f \left(x\right)$ is continuous,

$⇒ f \left({1}^{−}\right) =$f \left(1\right) = f\left({1}^{+}\right)$

$⇒ f \left(1\right) = 3 + c . . . \left($i\right)$

$⇒ $f\left({1}^{+}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}$2 \left($1 + h\right) + 1$

$⇒ $f\left({1}^{+}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}$3 + 2h = 3 . . . \left($ii\right)$

Using \left(i\$right)\text{and}\left(ii\right)$,

$⇒ c = 0$

At $x = 0, f \left($x\right)$ is continuous,

$⇒ f \left({0}^{−}\right) =$f \left($0\right) = $f\left({0}^{+}\right) . . . \left($iii\right)$

$⇒ f \left($0\right) = f \left({0}^{+}\right) =$2 . . . \left($iv\right)$

So, $f \left({0}^{−}\right)$has to be equal to $2$.

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{a - bcos\left(2h\right)}{h2}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{a - b \left\{1 - $\dfrac{4h^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{16h^{4}}{4 !} + . ..\right$\}}{h2}$

$⇒ \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{a - b + b\left\{2h^{2} - $\dfrac{2}{3}$h^{4} . ..\right\}}{h2}$

For limit to exist $a - b = 0$ and limit is $2b. . . \left($v\right)$

Using, \left(iii\right), \left(iv\right)\text{and}\left($v\right)$

$⇒ a = b = 1$

Checking differentiability at $x = 0$.

$⇒ LHD: \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\dfrac{1 - cos2h}{h2} -2}{- h}

$⇒ \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{4h^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{16h^{4}}{4 !} - . ..\right) -2h^{2}}{- h^{3}} =$0$

$⇒ RHD: \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\left(0 + h\right)2 + 2 - 2}{h} =$0$

Function is differentiable at every point in its domain

$∴ m = 0$

$⇒ m + a + b + c = 0 + 1 + 1 + 0$

$⇒ m + a + b + c = 2$

$

questions.q:
Let $f: R \to R$ be a function defined as

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{
5, ifx \le 1
a + bx, if1 < x < 3
b + 5x, if3 \le x < 5
30, ifx \ge 5
\right$

Then $f$ is:
options: not continuous for any values of $a$ and $b$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given function \(f: R → R\), such that \(f(x)=\left[$
5,if x \leq 1
a+b x,if 1 \lt x \lt 3
b+5 x,if 3 \leq x \lt 5
30,if x \geq 5
\right.\) If \(f\) is continuous at \(x=1\), then \(a+b=5\) ...(i) If \(f\) is continuous at \(x=3\), then \(\Rightarrow \quad $\begin{gathered}$a+3 b=b+15 \\ a+2 b=15 \quad \ldots (ii) \end{gathered}\) and if \(f\) is continuous at \(x=5\), then \(b+25=30 \Rightarrow b=5\) ...(iii) From Eqs. (ii) and (iii), we get \(a=5\) ...(iv) but \(a=5\) and \(b=5\) doesn't satisfy the Eq. (i). so, \(f: R → R\) is not continuous for any values of \(a\) and \(b\). Hence, option (4) is correct.$

questions.q: Let the function $f(x)=\left(x^2+1\right)\left|x^2-a x+2\right|+\cos |x|$ be not differentiable at the two points $x=\alpha=2$ and $x=\beta$. Then the distance of the point $(\alpha, \beta)$ from the line $12 x+5 y+10=0$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\left(x^2+1\right)\left|x^2-a x+2\right|+\cos |x|$ Notice that $\cos (-x)=\cos x=\cos |x|$ which means $\cos |x|$ is differentiable everywhere in $x \in R\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow f(x) \text { can be non differentiable where }\left|x^2-a x+2\right| \\ & =0 \end{aligned}\Rightarrow x^2-a x+2=0$
$\Rightarrow 4-2 a+2=0 \Rightarrow a=3\Rightarrow \quad\left(x^2-3 x+2\right)=0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x=1,2\beta=1$ distance of $(\alpha, \beta)$ from line $\begin{aligned} & 12 x+5 y+10=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{|2(12)+5(1)+10|}{13}=\frac{39}{13}=3 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left|2x^{2} + 5\left|x\right| - 3\right|, x \in R$. If $m$ and $n$ denote the number of points where $f$ is not continuous and not differentiable respectively, then $m + n$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \left|2x^{2} + 5\left|x\right| - 3\right|$

Now, let $y = \left|2x^{2} + 5x - 3\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|2x^{2} + 6x - x - 3\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|2x\left(x + 3\right) - \left(x + 3\right)\right|$

$⇒ y = \left|\left(2x - 1\right)\left(x + 3\right)\right|$

Graph of $⇒ y = \left|\left(2x - 1\right)\left(x + 3\right)\right|$ is given below:

Graph of $f\left(x\right) = \left|2x^{2} + 5\left|x\right| - 3\right|$ is given below:

So, $f \left(x\right)$ is continuous for $x \in R$ and non-differentiable at $x = \pm $\dfrac{1}{2},$0$

So, number of points of discontinuity$= 0 = m$

Also, number of points of non-discontinuity$= 3 = n$

$⇒ m + n = 3

$

questions.q:
$If the function& $f\left(x\right) = \left\{
\dfrac{1}{x}\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{x}{a}}{1 - \dfrac{x}{b}}\right),x 0
\right$

~is continuous at $x = 0,$~then $\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{4}{k}$is equal to :

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given that&

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{
\dfrac{1}{x}\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{x}{a}}{1 - \dfrac{x}{b}}\right),x 0
\right$

$f \left(x\right)$~is continuous at~$x = 0$

$L . H . L = R . H . L = f \left(0\right)$

$LHL = \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\dfrac{log\$left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{x}{a}}{1 - \dfrac{x}{b}}\right)}{x}$

$= \lim_{x \to ${0}^{-}}\dfrac{log \left(1 + \dfrac{x}{a}\right) -log \left(1 - \dfrac{x}{b}\right)}{x}$

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{-}}\dfrac{log \left(1 + $\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}{xa} \times $\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{log\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{b}\right)}{- \dfrac{x}{b}} \times - \dfrac{1}{b} = \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{a}

$RHL = \lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}\dfrac{\cos^{2}$x - \sin^{2}x - $1}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} -$1} \times $\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} + 1}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} + 1}

$= \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}} - $\dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{x2}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} + 1} +$1\right) = - 4$

So, \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{a} =$k = - 4 .$.

$k = - 4 ⇒ $\dfrac{4}{k} = -$1 .$

\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} = -$4 .$

$∴ $\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{4}{k} = -$5 .$

questions.q:
Let $g \left(x\right)$ be a linear function and $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}g \left(x\right), & x ≤ 0 \\ \left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}, \text{ and } x > 0\end{cases}\right$, is continuous at $x = 0$. If $f^{'} \left($1\right) = f \left(-$1\right)$, then the value of $g \left($3\right)$ is

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let, $g \left(x\right) = ax + b$

Now function $f\left(x\right)$ in continuous at $x = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f \left(x\right) = f \left(0\right)$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\$left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x} =$b$

$⇒ 0 = b$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = ax$

Now, for $x > 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \$left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}

$⇒ logf\left(x\right) = log\$left(\dfrac{1 + x}{2 + x}\right)\dfrac{1}{x}

$⇒ logf\left(x\right) = $\dfrac{log\left(1 + x\right) - log\left(2 + x\right)}{x}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{f\left(x\right)} \timesf^{'}\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x} - \dfrac{1}{2 + x}\right) - \left[log \left($1 + x\right) - $log\left($2 + x\right)\right]}{x2}

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right)\left\{\dfrac{x\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x} - \dfrac{1}{2 + x}\right) - \lleft[log\left(1 + x\right) - log\left(2 + x\right)\right]}{x2}\right\}$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(1\right) = f\left(1\$right)\left$\${\dfrac{ $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) - \left[$log\left(2\right) - log\left(3\right)\right]}{12}\right$\}$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(1\right) = $\dfrac{2}{3}\left$\{\dfrac{1}{6} --log\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\right\}

And, $f\left(-1\right) = g\left(-1\right) = - a$

$⇒ a = $\d$dfrac{2}{3}log\$left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{9}$

Now, finding g\left($3\right) = 3a + 0$

$⇒ $g\left($3\right) = $2log\$left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ g \left($3\right) = log $\$left(\dfrac{4}{9 ⋅ e^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}\right)

$

$= $\dfrac{a + 1}{2} +$1 . . . \left($3\right)$

$\lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}f\left($x\right) = \lim_{x \to ${0}^{+}}\dfrac{\sqrt{x + bx^{3}} - \sqrt{x}}{bx^{5 / 2}}

questions.q:
Let $f$ and $g$ be twice differentiable functions on $R$ such that

$f^{"}\left(x\right) = g^{"}\left(x\right) + 6x$

$f^{'}\left(1\right) = 4g^{'}\left(1\right) - 3 = 9$

$f\left(2\right) = 3g\left(2\right) = 12$

Then which of the following is NOT true ?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given functions are:

$f^{"} \left(x\right) = g^{"} \left($x\right) + 6x \ldots \left($1\right)$

$f^{'} \left($1\right) = 4g^{'} \left($1\right) - 3 = 9 \ldots \left($2\right)$

$f \left($2\right) = 3g \left($2\right) = 12 \ldots \left($3\right)$

By integrating~ \left($1\right)$, we get
$f^{'}\left($x\right) = g^{'}\left($x\right) + 3x^{2} + C$

At $x = 1$

$f^{'}\left($1\right) = g^{'}\left($1\right) + 3 + C$

$⇒ 9 = 3 + 3 + C ⇒ C = 3$

$∴ f^{'}\left($x\right) = g^{'}\left($x\right) + 3x^{2} + 3$

Again by integrating, we get

f\left($x\right) = $g\left($x\right) + x^{3} + 3x + D$

At $x = 2$, we get

f\left($2\right) = $g\left($2\right) + 8 + $3\left($2\right) + D$

$⇒ 12 = 4 + 8 + 6 + D ⇒ D = - 6$

So,

$f \left($x\right) = g \left($x\right) + x^{3} + 3x - 6$

Option~\left($A\right)$:

At $x = - 2$,

$⇒ g \left(-$2\right) - f \left(-$2\right) = 20$

So, this option is true.

Option~\left($B\right)$

If~$- 1 < x < 2$

Let~$h\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) = x^{3} + 3x - 6$

$⇒ h^{'}\left(x\right) = 3x^{2} + 3$

$⇒ h ' \left(x\right) > 0$~for all values of~$x$.

So, $h\left(-1\right) < h\left(x\right) < h\left(2\right)$

$⇒ - 10 < h\left(x\right) < 8$

$⇒ \left|h \left($x\right)\right| < 10$~ ~ ~

So, this option is NOT true.

Option~\left(C\right)$

$h^{'}\left(x\right) = f^{'}\left(x\right) - g^{'}\left(x\right) = 3x^{2} + 3$

If \left|h^{'}\left(x\right)\right| < 6 ⇒ \left|3x^{2} + 3\right| < 6$

$⇒ 3x^{2} + 3 < 6$~and~$- 6 < 3x^{2} + 3$

$⇒ x^{2} < 1$~and~$x^{2} > - 3 \left(alwaystrue\right)$

$⇒ - 1 < x < 1$~ ~ ~

So,~If $x \in \left(-1, 1\right)$~then~\left|f^{'} \left($x\right) - g^{'} \left(x\right)\right| < 6$

So, this option is true.

Option~\left(D\right)$

$f\left(x\right) - g\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ x^{3} + 3x - 6 = 0$

$h\left(x\right) = x^{3} + 3x - 6$

Here, $h\left(1\right) = - ve$~and $h \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = +$ve$

So, there exists ${x}_{0} \in \left($1, $\dfrac{3}{2}\right) such that~$f \left({x}_{0}\right) =$g \left({x}_{0}\right)$ \text{ and }

So, this option is true.

$

questions.q: Let $f\left(x\right) = min\left\{1, 1 + xsinx\right\}, 0 \le x \le 2\pi$. If~$m$ is the number of points, where~$f$ is not differentiable and $n$~is the number of points, where~$f$ is not continuous, then the ordered pair  \left(m, n\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x\right) = min \left$\{1, 1 + xsinx\right\}x \in \left[$0, $2\pi\right]

f\left($x\right) = \left$\{
1, 0 ≤ x $\le \pi$
1 + xsinx, $\pi \le$x $\le2\pi$
\right$

Now, at $x = $\pi, \lim_{x \to {π}^{-}}$f \left($x\right) = 1 = \lim_{x \to {π}^{+}}f\left($x\right)$

$∴ f \left(x\right)$ is continuous in \left[0, 2\pi\right]$

So, number of points of discontinuity is zero or~$n = 0$

Now, at $x = \pi$

L.H.D $= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(\pi - h\right) - f\left(\pi\right)}{- h} = 0$

R.H.D $= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(\pi + h\right) - f\left(\pi\right)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{1 - \left(\pi +h\right)sinh - 1}{h}$

$= - \pi$

$∴ f\left(x\right)$ is not differentiable at $x = \pi$~so,~$m = 1$

$∴ \left(m, n\right) = \left(1, 0\right)

$

questions.solution:
$f ( x )$ is differentiable then will also continuous then~$f ( \pi ) = {k}_{1}\left(\pi - \pi\right)2 - 1 = - 1$

$f\left({π}^{+}\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}{k}_{2}cos \left(\pi +$h\right) = - {k}_{2}$

then,~$f ' \left({π}^{-}\right) ==2{k}_{1}\left(\pi - \pi\right) =$0$

~$⇒ f ' \left({π}^{-}\right) =f ' \left({π}^{+}\right) =0$

Similarly,~we get

$f ' ' ( x ) = \left\{\begin{cases}2{k}_{1}, & x \le \pi\\ - {k}_{2}cosx, & x > \pi\end{cases}\right$

As the function is twice differentiable, the second-order derivatives, $LHD = RHD$~

Let $f: R \to R$ be defined as

where \left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. If $f$ is continuous at $x = 2$, then $\lambda + \mu$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$If& $f \left(x\right)$~is continuous at~$x = 2$, then~$\lim_{x \to {2}^{+}}f \left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to {2}^{-}}f \left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to 2}f\left(x\right)$

Here,

$\lim_{x \to {2}^{+}}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to ${2}^{+}}e\dfrac{tan ( x - 2 )}{x - 2} =e^{1} = e$

$\lim_{x \to {2}^{-}}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to ${2}^{-}}\dfrac{\lambda\left|$x^{2} - 5x + 6\right|}{\mu\left(5x - x^{2} - 6\right)} = \lim_{x \to ${2}^{-}}\dfrac{- \lambda ($x - 2 ) ( x - 3 )}{\mu ( x - 2 ) ( x - 3 )} = - $\dfrac{λ}{μ}

\left(∵ \left|x^{2} - 5x + 6\right| = \left\{
\left($x - 2\right)\left(x - 3\right)if x 3
- \left($x - 2\right) \left(x - 3\right)if 2 < x < 3
\right\right)$

For continuity $\mu = e = - \dfrac{λ}{μ}⇒ \mu = e, \lambda = - e^{2}$

$\lambda + \mu = e ( - e + 1 )$

$

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\dfrac{\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1 - x + x^{2}\right) + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1 + x + x^{2}\right)}{secx - cosx}, & x \in \left(\dfrac{- \pi}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right) -\left$\{0\right\} \\ k \text{ and } , x = 0\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{\lleft(ln\left($1 + x^{2} + x^{4}\right)\right)cosx}{1 - \cos^{2}x} =$k$

Taking L.H.S$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\l$left(ln\left($1 + x^{2} + x^{4}\right)\right)cosx}{1 - \cos^{2}x}

$= \lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{ln\left(1 + x^{2} + x^{4}\right)}{x^{2} + x^{4}}\rright)x^{2} \left($1 + x^{2}\$right)cosx}{\left(\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{x2}\right)$x^{2}}

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \left(\dfrac{ln \left($1 + x^{2} + x^{4}\right)}${x^{2} + x^{4}}\right)\left(1 + x^{2}\right)cosx $\$left(\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{x2}\right)

$= \left(1\right)\left(1 + 0\right)1\left(1\right) = 1$

questions.q: Let& $f ( x ) = x \cdot  \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\right],$for~$- 10 < x < 10,$ where~\left[t\right]$ denotes the greatest integer function. Then the number of points of discontinuity of~$f  \left(x\right)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that the greatest integer function is discontinuous at integral points.

$- 5 < \dfrac{x}{2} < 5$

$⇒ \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\right] = - 5, - 4, - 3, - 2, - 1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$, are the integer values.

At~$x = 0$,~$f\left({0}^{+}\right) = f\left(0\right) = f\left({0}^{-}\right) = 0$, which means that function is continuous at~$x = 0$.

$∵ x \ne - 10 ⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} \ne - 5$

Hence, the function is discontinuous at points~$- 4, - 3, - 2, - 1, 1, 2, 3, 4$

The number of values is~$8$ .

So, finding LHD and RHD at $x = 2$ we get,

$- $\dfrac{1}{x2} =$2ax$

$⇒ $\dfrac{- 1}{4} =$4a$

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{- 1}{16}

Now, for function to be continuous at $x = 2$ we get,

questions.q:
Let $f: R \to R$ be a function defined as~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3\left(1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) & \text{if} & | x | \le 2 \\ 0 & \text{if} & | x | > 2\end{cases}\right .$

Let $g: R \to R$ be given by $g ( x ) = f ( x + 2 ) - f ( x - 2 ) .$~If $n$ and $m$ denote the number of points in $R$ where $g$ is not continuous and not differentiable, respectively, then $n + m$ is equal to ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given function is& $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}3 \left($1 - \dfrac{| x |}{2}\right) \text{ and } if \text{ and } | x | ≤ 2 \\ 0 \text{ and } if \text{ and } | x | > 2\end{cases}\right$

By using the definition of modulus function, we have~\left|$x\right| = \left$\${\begin{cases}x, & x ≥ 0 \\ - x, & x < 0\end{cases}\right$~and also, we know that if~\left|x\right| \le a, ⇒ - a \le x \le a$~and if~\left|x\right| > a, ⇒ x a,$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = \left$\{\begin{cases}3 \left(1 + $\dfrac{x}{2}\right),$ \text{ and } - 2 ≤ x ≤ 0 \\ 3 \left(1 - $\dfrac{x}{2}\right),$ \text{ and } 0 xorx > 2\end{cases}\right$

Now,~$f\left(x - 2\right) = \left\${\begin{cases}3\left(1 + \dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right),& - 2 ≤ x - 2 ≤ 0 \\ 3 \left($1 - $\dfrac{x - 2}{2}\right),$ \text{ and } 0 x - 2orx - 2 > 2\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ $f\left($x - 2\right) = \left$\{\$begin{cases}\dfrac{3x}{2},$ \text{ and } 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 \\ 6 - $\dfrac{3x}{2},$ \text{ and } 2 xorx > 4\end{cases}\right$

And,~f\left($x + 2\right) = \left$\{\$begin{cases}3\left($1 + $\dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right),$ \text{ and } - 2 ≤ x + 2 ≤ 0 \\ 3 \left($1 - $\dfrac{x + 2}{2}\right),$ \text{ and } 0 x + 2orx + 2 > 2\end{cases}\right$

$⇒ $f\left($x + 2\right) = \left$\{\begin{cases}6 + $\dfrac{3x}{2},$ \text{ and } - 4 ≤ x $\le -$2 \\ - $\dfrac{3x}{2},$ \text{ and } - 2 xorx > 0\end{cases}\right$

Hence, g\left($x\right) = $f\left($x + 2\right) - $f\left($x - 2\right) = \left$\{
$\dfrac{3x}{2} +$6, - 4 ≤ x $\le -$2
- $\dfrac{3x}{2}, -$2 < x < 2
$\dfrac{3x}{2} -$6, 2 ≤ x ≤ 4
0, x \in ( - $\infty , -$4 ) ∪ ( 4, $\infty )$
\right$

The graph of~$g \left(x\right)$~is given below

From the graph we can observe that the function~$g \left($x\right)$~is continuous everywhere, hence the number of points where~$g \left(x\right)$~is not continuos is~$n = 0$~and the graph has sharp corners at the points~ \left(-4, 0\right), \left(4, 0\right), \left(-$2, 3\right) \text{ and } \left($2, - 3\right)$~thus the number of points where~$g \left(x\right)$~is not differentiable are~$m = 4$

$⇒ n + m = 4 .$

$
